plan: In a sealed-bid auction with rational bidders and values between $0 and $49, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected average of the competitors' bids. Given my value of $40, I should bid close to this value but lower to ensure profit if I win. A bid of $39.9 maximizes my chance of winning while ensuring a profit if the second-highest bid is below $39.9.

To maximize profit, bid slightly below the value ($13) to ensure a win if others bid lower. Rational bidders aim to bid less than their value to avoid negative profit. Assuming others bid around their values, I'll bid slightly below mine to win and pay less than $13. A bid of $12.8 balances winning likelihood and profit margin.

Given my value of $17 for the prize, I aim to bid slightly below my value to maximize potential profit while considering rational competitors. Bidding $16.9 maximizes potential profit if competitors bid below my value. This strategy balances winning probability and profit, considering rational bidders will likely bid close to their values.
